_meta.description: Categorical French elision: the final vowel (a, e, or i) of a closed set of short grammatical words is dropped and replaced by an apostrophe when the following token begins with a vowel or h muet. Elision is suspended before h aspiré words (see h_aspire.json) and before huit, huitième, onze, onzième and their derivatives, where the full form is kept.
_meta.trigger_rule: Elision fires when the eliding word is immediately followed by a token whose first letter is a, e, i, o, u, y, or a silent h (h muet) -- i.e. any orthographic vowel, or an h that itself does not block liaison/elision. It is suspended (full form kept, no apostrophe) before h aspiré words (h_aspire.json) and before huit, huitième, onze, onzième and their derivatives.
_meta.source: https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/21737/lorthographe/elision-et-apostrophe/elision-obligatoire (cases where elision is mandatory); https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/21745/lorthographe/elision-et-apostrophe/elision-interdite (cases where elision is forbidden)

le.category: definite article (masc. sg.) / 3rd person singular direct-object clitic pronoun
le.source: BDL 21737 -- "la voyelle finale d'un mot" is elided in le, la before verbs/nouns starting with vowel or h muet

la.category: definite article (fem. sg.) / 3rd person singular direct-object clitic pronoun
la.note: does not elide before h aspiré (la hache, not l'hache) or before huit/onze (la onzième heure is not elided in this idiomatic set)

me.category: 1st person singular object/reflexive clitic (placed before the verb)

te.category: 2nd person singular object/reflexive clitic (placed before the verb)

se.category: 3rd person reflexive clitic (placed before the verb)

de.category: preposition (also base of the partitive/indefinite determiner)
de.example: un vent d'hiver, un ami d'ami

que.category: relative pronoun / subordinating conjunction, including compounds (bien que, après que, parce que, jusqu'à ce que...)

si.condition: elides ONLY before il / ils (s'il, s'ils) -- never before elle, elles, on, or any other word (si elle, si on, si une... are never elided)
si.source: BDL 21737 -- "il y a élision du i de si devant les pronoms il et ils uniquement"
